contradictions.what: Rep says it was purely a price loss, then concedes Martin would still see 'same rate', so maybe not only the rate.
Rep says nothing bombed and it was a good cycle, yet no customer-specific value case existed and Lucy's business-case request went unmet.
Rep thought Lucy was sold and no analysis needed, but Lucy had called it a formality and was then surprised by the CFO.
Rep says matching price would win, but also notes IT hesitation and the same-thing framing, which price alone may not fix.
Rep says the comparison is unfair and the offerings differ, yet did not get that difference onto the page.

dodges.question: Which part of our pitch got a reaction, and which got silence?
dodges.what: Said 'Silence, honestly, nothing bombed' and moved to 'we lost on price'; later gaps (no business case, no figure) contradict it.

dodges.question: Did we put a figure on the value they'd get?
dodges.what: Answered with the generic uplift slide; admitted a Fernbrook figure was absent only after being pressed.

dodges.question: So what did Martin have in front of him about what one in twelve orders was costing?
dodges.what: Hesitated, said 'Nothing from us', and fell back on assuming Lucy told him.

dodges.question: If we had matched the price, would we have won? What else would have needed to be true?
dodges.what: Said 'Yes. Probably' then listed other factors and hedged with 'maybe not only the rate'.

outcome_signals.what: Deal lost; rep attributes it to price after the CFO refused to pay more.
CFO said no; the rep never met him and learned this via Lucy.
Incumbent bank sharpened its rate; the customer stayed with it, so the whole deal appears lost, not partial.
IT was wary of moving before spring but would proceed if finance approved; timing risk remained.
